title: The Energy Consumption of Blockchain Technology: Beyond Myth

authors.name: Johannes Sedlmeir
authors.affiliation: Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Information Technology

abstract: Abstract When talking about blockchain technology in academia, business, and society, frequently generalizations are still heared about its – supposedly inherent – enormous energy consumption. This perception inevitably raises concerns about the further adoption of blockchain technology, a fact that inhibits rapid uptake of what is widely considered to be a groundbreaking and disruptive innovation. However, blockchain technology is far from homogeneous, meaning that blanket statements about its energy consumption should be reviewed with care. The article is meant to bring clarity to the topic in a holistic fashion, looking beyond claims regarding the energy consumption of Bitcoin, which have, so far, dominated the discussion.

The Energy Consumption of Blockchain Technology: Beyond Myth (2020) in Business & Information Systems Engineering is authored by Johannes Sedlmeir, Hans Ulrich Buhl and Gilbert Fridgen. Topics: Blockchain, CLARITY, Consumption (sociology), Homogeneous and Meaning (existential).

500 citations (OpenAlex). Citations peaked in 2024 with 95 citing works. Citing venues include Sustainability, IEEE Access and Energies.
